plan.contextChunk: This figure depicts a three-dimensional schematic of a 1D convolutional layer with multiple channels, rendered in a 3D perspective with labeled axes for Channels, Width, and Height. The input layer H and output layer H' are shown as two 3D volumetric grids of white circles with black outlines and thin strokes, each circle representing a feature value at a specific (channel, position) coordinate; the two grids are positioned side by side with spatial offset to convey depth. Between the input and output grids, the weight tensor Omega is represented as a smaller 3D grid of circles, and two operator symbols in terracotta color (#b46d59) — a circled-cross (otimes, indicating convolution) and a circled-plus (oplus, indicating bias addition) — are placed between the input, weights, and output to denote the two arithmetic steps. Dark slate (#424b4f) arrows connect the input volume to the weight tensor and from there to the output volume, showing the flow of computation; additional terracotta triangle-tipped arrows indicate the direction of individual connections between feature channels. This figure demonstrates how a 1D convolution with multiple input and output channels operates as a weighted linear combination across channel and spatial dimensions, extending the single-channel 1D convolution to multi-channel feature maps.

elements: Input tensor H: 3D grid of white spheres with thin dark outlines (Width along +X, Height along +Y, Channels along +Z)
Highlighted receptive-field slab in H: a semi-transparent gray box enclosing a kernel-width x 1-height x all-channels slice of spheres at the leftmost width position
Convolution operator symbol (circled-cross, otimes) in terracotta between H and the weights
Weight tensor Omega: 3D block of small colored cubes (kernel-width along +X, input-channels along +Z) representing the filter for the currently selected output channel
Bias/addition operator symbol (circled-plus, oplus) in terracotta between the weights and H'
Output tensor H': 3D grid of white spheres with thin dark outlines (output-width along +X, Height along +Y, output-channels along +Z)
One highlighted output sphere (gray fill) at the computed (position, height, selected-channel) coordinate in H'
Axis label arrows in dark slate: 'Width' receding along +X, 'Height' vertical along +Y, 'Channels' receding along +Z, drawn at the input tensor
Text labels 'Input layer, H', 'Weights, Omega', 'Output layer, H'

interactions.teaches: Rotating the whole scene lets the learner read off which physical direction carries Width, Height, and Channels, confirming that the convolution slides along Width while mixing across Channels

interactions.label: Kernel width k
interactions.teaches: Widening the kernel lengthens the gray receptive-field slab along the Width axis of H and shrinks the output width of H' to W - k + 1, showing the trade-off between spatial context and output resolution

interactions.label: Output channel c
interactions.teaches: Each output channel is produced by its own distinct filter slice in Omega; stepping c recolors the weight block and re-highlights the corresponding depth plane in H', revealing that channels are mixed independently per output map

demo_steps.title: Default 1D conv
demo_steps.narration: With k=3 the gray slab spans three width positions across all six input channels; the matching 3x6 weight block is dotted with the input to emit one highlighted value in H'.

demo_steps.title: Widen the kernel
demo_steps.narration: Increase k to 6: the receptive field now covers most of the Width axis and the output tensor H' visibly narrows to W - k + 1 columns.

demo_steps.title: Switch output channel
demo_steps.narration: Move c to 2: a different filter slice in Omega lights up and a different depth plane of H' is highlighted, showing each output channel has its own learned weights.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World mapping: +X = Width, +Y = Height, +Z = Channels (depth receding diagonal). Input H: Width W=8, Height=6, Channels C_in=6; spheres radius ~0.16, spacing 0.42, centered near x=-4.5. Receptive-field slab = k (X) x 1 (Y) x 6 (Z) semi-transparent gray #9aa0a3 box at leftmost width index, enclosing the matching spheres (tint them gray). Weights Omega centered near x=0: cubes size ~0.34 laid out k (X) x 6 (Z) for the selected output channel, terracotta palette [#d99873,#5a2d20,#a85a40,#f3d9b8,#8a4a35,#3d1f16] cycling per cube; recolor/rebuild when outputChannel changes (C_out=4 distinct palettes). Output H' centered near x=+4.5: output-width = W-k+1 (X) x 6 (Y) x C_out=4 (Z) spheres; highlight the sphere at (width index 0, height 0, selected channel) with gray #9aa0a3 fill. Operator glyphs as flat ring+cross / ring+plus sprites in #b46d59 placed between blocks at mid-height. Axis arrows #424b4f. White spheres #ffffff with outline #1a1a1a. Overall scene spans roughly x in [-6.5, 6.5], y in [-1.5, 1.5], z in [-1.5, 1.5].
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE.InstancedMesh for the sphere grids (input and output) for performance; recolor instances for the receptive-field tint and the highlighted output sphere rather than rebuilding. Rebuild the Omega cube block and the output-tensor X-extent reactively on kernelWidth/outputChannel change. Render operator glyphs as canvas-texture sprites so they always face the camera during orbit. Keep orbit constrained so the axonometric reading of the three axes stays legible.

interactions.teaches: Each output channel is produced by its own distinct filter slice in Omega; stepping c recolors the weight block and re-highlights the corresponding depth plane in H', revealing that channels are mixed independently per output map

demo_steps.title: Default 1D conv
demo_steps.narration: With k=3 the gray slab spans three width positions across all six input channels; the matching 3x6 weight block is dotted with the input to emit one highlighted value in H'.

demo_steps.title: Widen the kernel
demo_steps.narration: Increase k to 6: the receptive field now covers most of the Width axis and the output tensor H' visibly narrows to W - k + 1 columns.

demo_steps.title: Switch output channel
demo_steps.narration: Move c to 2: a different filter slice in Omega lights up and a different depth plane of H' is highlighted, showing each output channel has its own learned weights.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World mapping: +X = Width, +Y = Height, +Z = Channels (depth receding diagonal). Input H: Width W=8, Height=6, Channels C_in=6; spheres radius ~0.16, spacing 0.42, centered near x=-4.5. Receptive-field slab = k (X) x 1 (Y) x 6 (Z) semi-transparent gray #9aa0a3 box at leftmost width index, enclosing the matching spheres (tint them gray). Weights Omega centered near x=0: cubes size ~0.34 laid out k (X) x 6 (Z) for the selected output channel, terracotta palette [#d99873,#5a2d20,#a85a40,#f3d9b8,#8a4a35,#3d1f16] cycling per cube; recolor/rebuild when outputChannel changes (C_out=4 distinct palettes). Output H' centered near x=+4.5: output-width = W-k+1 (X) x 6 (Y) x C_out=4 (Z) spheres; highlight the sphere at (width index 0, height 0, selected channel) with gray #9aa0a3 fill. Operator glyphs as flat ring+cross / ring+plus sprites in #b46d59 placed between blocks at mid-height. Axis arrows #424b4f. White spheres #ffffff with outline #1a1a1a. Overall scene spans roughly x in [-6.5, 6.5], y in [-1.5, 1.5], z in [-1.5, 1.5].
interactionPlan.notes: Use THREE.InstancedMesh for the sphere grids (input and output) for performance; recolor instances for the receptive-field tint and the highlighted output sphere rather than rebuilding. Rebuild the Omega cube block and the output-tensor X-extent reactively on kernelWidth/outputChannel change. Render operator glyphs as canvas-texture sprites so they always face the camera during orbit. Keep orbit constrained so the axonometric reading of the three axes stays legible.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure depicts a three-dimensional schematic of a 1D convolutional layer with multiple channels, rendered in a 3D perspective with labeled axes for Channels, Width, and Height. The input layer H and output layer H' are shown as two 3D volumetric grids of white circles with black outlines and thin strokes, each circle representing a feature value at a specific (channel, position) coordinate; the two grids are positioned side by side with spatial offset to convey depth. Between the input and output grids, the weight tensor Omega is represented as a smaller 3D grid of circles, and two operator symbols in terracotta color (#b46d59) — a circled-cross (otimes, indicating convolution) and a circled-plus (oplus, indicating bias addition) — are placed between the input, weights, and output to denote the two arithmetic steps. Dark slate (#424b4f) arrows connect the input volume to the weight tensor and from there to the output volume, showing the flow of computation; additional terracotta triangle-tipped arrows indicate the direction of individual connections between feature channels. This figure demonstrates how a 1D convolution with multiple input and output channels operates as a weighted linear combination across channel and spatial dimensions, extending the single-channel 1D convolution to multi-channel feature maps.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for channel index: step through output channels in H', highlighting the corresponding filter slice in the weights Ω and showing how each input channel of H contributes to that output
- Drag to rotate the 3D tensor blocks: adjust the viewing angle of H, Ω, and H' together to inspect the Channels, Width, and Height axes from different orientations
- Slider for kernel width: vary the convolution kernel size along the Width axis and show how the receptive field span changes in the input H and how the output H' dimensions update accordingly
